To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
metamodel driven model extractions from dynamic systems are feasible and that the resulting models can be jointly used with the models extracted from static systems.
Metamodels can be automatically generated from legacy systems and that the generated metamodels can be used to extract abstract models from legacy systems.
(i) the metamodel of a programming language may be used to drive model extraction from legacy systems, and (ii) models of dynamic systems may be extracted from the execution traces of these systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following issues: (1) How can we extract a model of a system at run time, (2) How can we make this extraction process metamodel-driven, (3) How can we use this extracted model to drive the evolution of the system, (4) What kind of models can be extracted and (5) what kind of models can we extract at runtime?
the following questions: How can models be extracted from legacy software? How can models be used for reverse engineering and software evolution

How can we extract models from legacy systems? How can we use models extracted from legacy systems in the context of reverse engineering and of software evolution?

model extraction is a very complex problem that may be addressed in several ways, but the most interesting ones are probably metamodel driven model extractions from both static and dynamic systems.

model extraction is a very difficult task but that it may be feasible in certain ideal conditions.
